REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - NOVEMBER 9, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
NOVEMBER 9, 2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by City of Cerritos Recreation Services Youth
  Flag Football League, pee-wee division team, “Packers.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  None.

5B.  Ratification of Mayor’s Appointment to the Bellflower Unified School District
  Citizen’s Task Force.

  This item was continued to the next City Council meeting.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Surya Villarino, CPE Tot Lot President, spoke regarding the Cerritos Park East Tot
  Lot room allocations.

  Emily Chen-Darnell spoke regarding the Cerritos Park East Tot Lot program.

  Paul Bellenbaum spoke regarding the book titled, “Act of War.”

  John Darnell spoke regarding the Cerritos Park East Tot Lot room allocations.

  Jake Velazquez thanked the Cerritos Sherriff Station for hosting the Cerritos
  Haunted Jail and thanked the Department of Parks and Recreation for hosting the
  Cerritos Halloween Festival.

  Tom Tislow spoke in regards to the closure of the VFW Frank Garcia Post 1846,
  the Cerritos Veterans Memorial and the recent NFL protests.

  Murali Vasudevan encouraged residents to tour the Cerritos Astor Museum
  Staging Facility, spoke regarding the Public Records Act process, requested a
  follow-up on Council action items, and commended the City on items on the
  current agenda.
 City of Cerritos  November 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Nick Duvally, Local Fire Chief, notified the business community of current fire
  inspection scams circulating the local area.

  Christopher Craig, representative from the office of Assemblymember Cristina
  Garcia, invited the community to participate in the “There Ought to be a Law”
  contest.

  Murali Vasudevan requested clarification of various line items on the Register of
  Demands and requested clarification on a line item appearing on the
  Treasurer’s Report.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  October 26, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of October 26, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Registers of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 9,
  2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Registers of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  11/09/2017 $6,492,765.58  (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  November 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s Report for the period ending September 30,
  2017 (COUNCIL).

  Approval of the Successor Agency’s Treasurer’s Report for the period ending
  September 30, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending September 30, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and discussion of potential conversion of residential street lights from
  existing high pressure sodium vapor (HPSV) to light emitting diode (LED)
  technology (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Rafudeen, Electric Utility Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed support for the project, commended staff for the
  thorough report, requested the City look into related subsides and suggested a
  secure community survey.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Ratify the Southern California Edison (SCE) Company Schedule LS-1 Option E,
  Energy Efficient-Light Emitting Diode (LED) Fixture Replacement Rate
  Agreement between the City of Cerritos and the Southern California Edison
  Company, administratively submitted by staff; and
  2. Authorize the implementation of the demonstration project at Cerritos Sports
  Complex; and
  3. Direct staff to conduct a survey to select street light color and wattage level
  and bring back a report to Council (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  November 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS GRANTING AN EASEMENT DEED TO
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON FOR UTILITY PURPOSES AT THE LINCOLN
  STATION COMMERCIAL PROPERTY LOCATED AT 11900 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS,
  CA, 90703 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full reading
  of and adopt Resolution No. 2017-31, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS GRANTING AN EASEMENT DEED TO
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON FOR UTILITY PURPOSES AT THE
  LINCOLN STATION COMMERCIAL PROPERTY LOCATED AT 11900 SOUTH
  STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703 (APN 7054-024-060) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  An informational report on the City’s reforestation program and tree removal policy
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Steven Pirus, independent certified arborist, spoke regarding arboriculture, tree care
  practices and structure, and noted that the quality of the City’s trees meets ISA
  (International Society of Arboriculture) quality standards.

  Murali Vasudevan commended the City for addressing the reforestation program,
  encouraged the City to maintain the number of trees it has and requested the City
  be proactive with tree maintenance.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.
 City of Cerritos  November 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Direct staff to engage the Property Preservation Commission to review the removal
  and replacement of problematic tree species, such as Pine Trees; and
  2. Direct staff to engage the Property Preservation Commission to conduct a public
  hearing and make any recommended edits to the City’s tree removal and trimming
  policy, which may include consideration of tree removals based on the financial
  burden for the resident (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of playground equipment at Loma Park (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherré Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the “Shine”
  color palette for the playground equipment at Loma Park (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Solanki, and Edwards,
  Mayor Pro Tem Pulido, and Mayor Hu.

  CONSENSUS (Pulido): Directed staff to bring back a report reviewing the
  Cerritos Park East facility usage policy as it relates to the Tot Lot program.
 City of Cerritos  November 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:38 p.m.

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
